name: Timely Filing MTF.2 — Member Timely Filing Exceeded Navigator

steps.hint: Click the 'Event Resolution' tab. The Active Edit panel shows PX_MTF — 'Member timely filing' flagged as a Hard Edit (red). That is the event you must resolve.
steps.name: Identify the PX_MTF hard edit on Event Resolution
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. All edits on the claim are listed; the PX_MTF edit ('Member timely filing') is the active Hard Edit, flagged in red. That is the current event you are resolving.
steps.checklistItem: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_MTF hard edit identified
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.

steps.hint: Open the 'Notes' tab and read the BEN field in the Task Management section — it reads SPIDER, so proceed.
steps.name: Identify the benefit type
steps.description: Determine the benefit type by navigating to the Notes tab, then the Task Management section, and reviewing the BEN field. If the BEN field indicates WPD, follow the alternate SOP steps. If the BEN field indicates SPIDER, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the BEN field displays SPIDER; therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Notes tab to read the BEN field.

steps.hint: Open 'Search' → 'Benefits', scroll to Plan options, and read the MEMBER CLAIM FILING DAY LIMIT row — the Maximum is 365 days.
steps.name: Look up the Timely Filing Limit
steps.description: Determine the timely filing limit by navigating to the Search tab, then the Benefits sub-tab, and reviewing the Plan Level section. Locate the MEMBER CLAIM FILING DAY LIMIT entry and review the value displayed in the Maximum field to identify the timely filing limit. In this scenario, the Maximum field displays 365 days; therefore, the timely filing limit (TFL) is 365 days.
steps.checklistItem: Look up the Timely Filing Limit
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Benefits sub-tab inside Search to read the Plan options.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Details'. Claim type is Professional and ITS Home is No — the claim is Non-ITS Home, so proceed.
steps.name: Verify the claim is Non-ITS Home
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is ITS Home by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and reviewing the Additional Claim Data section. If the claim type is identified as ITS Home, follow the alternate SOP steps. If the claim type is Non-ITS Home, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional, which is classified as Non-ITS Home. Therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the claim is Non-ITS Home
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Details sub-tab inside Claim Data to read the claim type and ITS Home flag.

steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' and look in the All Edits section — the PX_PAJ event is present. Check the Claim Header's Frequency next.
steps.name: Check for the PX_PAJ event
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains a corrected claim event by looking for the PX_PAJ event in the Event Resolution tab. In this scenario, the PX_PAJ event is present, so the next condition (the Frequency value) must also be checked before concluding whether the claim is a corrected claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab to look for the PX_PAJ event.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' and check the Frequency field under General Claim Data. It is not 7 — so even with the PX_PAJ event this is not a corrected claim, and the trainee proceeds.
steps.name: Confirm the Frequency value
steps.description: Confirm the Frequency value by navigating to the Claim Header tab, then the General Claim Data section. A claim is considered a corrected claim when a PX_PAJ event is present and the Frequency field is set to 7. When both conditions are met, the alternate SOP for corrected claims must be followed. If either condition is not met, the claim is not considered a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step. In this scenario, the Frequency value is not 7. Therefore, the claim is not a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab to confirm the Frequency value.

steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' again and scan the All Edits section for a PX_SUT event — there is none, so the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds.
steps.name: Check for the PX_SUT event
steps.description: Determine whether the provider is Sutter by looking for the PX_SUT event in the Event Resolution tab. If the PX_SUT event is present, follow the Sutter procedure; if it is absent, the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds. In this scenario, the PX_SUT event is absent, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab again to look for the PX_SUT event.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' again and check the Provider participation field under General Claim Data. It reads Non-PAR — so proceed.
steps.name: Verify provider participation status
steps.description: Verify the claim type and provider status by navigating to the Claim Header tab, then the Provider Information section, and reviewing the Provider Participation field. The claim type has already been confirmed as Professional. To proceed, the Provider Participation field must display Non PAR, indicating that the provider is non-participating. If the claim type is Professional and the provider status is Non PAR, continue to the next step. Otherwise, follow the alternate SOP.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab again to verify the Provider participation field.

steps.hint: Open 'Claim Lines'. Each line's Service from date (03/05/2025, 02/10/2025, 01/15/2025) is more than 365 days before the claim summary Receipt date (03/09/2026) — all three are outside the TFL, so proceed.
steps.name: Note the Service from dates & calculate the filing window against the TFL
steps.description: Go to the Claim Lines tab and note the Service from date of each of the three claim lines. Then note the Receipt date from the claim summary and calculate the difference between each claim line's Service from date and the Receipt date — three separate calculations, one per claim line. If a claim line's difference is within the 365-day TFL, that line is within the TFL; if it exceeds the TFL, the line is outside. If all claim lines are within the TFL, follow the alternate SOP steps; if any line is outside, proceed. In this scenario, all three claim lines fall outside the 365-day TFL, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.checklistItem: Note the Service from dates & calculate the filing window against the TFL
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Lines tab. The Receipt-date-minus-Service-from calculation for each line is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).

steps.hint: Open 'Search' → 'Claims', enter the Service to date, and click 'Search'. Two claims appear — open the Resolved-Cancelled claim's member information; the Finalization code PX_RDELEP shows it was previously deleted.
steps.name: Look up prior deleted claims
steps.description: Review the member's claim history to check whether the same claim was previously deleted because it was submitted with incorrect data or because the provider data was not loaded at the time. First view the member information then navigate to the Search tab → Claims sub-tab — the Service from date, HCID, and Provider Tax ID are auto-populated. Enter the Service to date and click Search. Two matching claims are listed — one active claim with status Pending-Investigation and one with status Resolved-Cancelled. Open the Resolved-Cancelled claim's member information; if the Finalization code field shows PX_RDELEP, the claim was previously deleted.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Search on the Search → Claims sub-tab, which dispatches the claims_search action and reveals the two matching claims.

steps.hint: Click 'View member information' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, then 'Open claim detail' in the dialog. The gap between its claim line's Service from date and Receipt date exceeds 365 days — the deleted claim was outside the TFL, so it does not qualify and the trainee proceeds with rejection.
steps.name: Verify the deleted claim's filing window
steps.description: To verify whether a deleted claim was filed within the timely filing limit, select View Member Information from the applicable deleted claim record, then click Open Claim Detail. Review the deleted claim details, which are displayed in the same format as the current claim. Locate the Service From Date and the Receipt Date, then calculate the difference between these dates. If the filing period falls within the 365-day timely filing limit (TFL), the deleted claim qualifies as being filed within the TFL and the alternate SOP steps must be followed. If no deleted claim is found that was filed within the 365-day TFL, proceed with rejection. In this scenario, the deleted claim was filed outside the 365-day TFL. Therefore, it does not qualify, and the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the deleted claim's filing window
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks 'Open claim detail' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, which dispatches the open_prior_claim action. The 365-day calculation is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).

steps.hint: Open 'Attachment' → 'Attachments' and review the PWK section. The Type and Document number fields are empty — no Acceptable Proof was received, so proceed to reject the claim.
steps.name: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section
steps.description: Check whether Acceptable Proof has been received to override the TFL. Navigate to the Attachments tab → Attachments sub-tab and review the PWK section. If a proof document has been submitted, the Type and Document number fields are populated. If proof has been received and approved, follow the alternate SOP steps; if no proof has been received or it has not been approved, proceed to reject the claim. In this scenario, no proof has been received, so the trainee proceeds to reject the claim.
steps.checklistItem: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Attachments sub-tab on the Attachment tab to review the PWK section.

steps.hint: Action menu → Deny Claim. Enter reject code PX_R24040 in the Deny Claim section, click Submit, then confirm the pop-up.
steps.name: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_R24040
steps.description: Because the rejection is being applied at the claim level, use reject code PX_R24040 in accordance with the SOP. Select Action Menu from the claim header, then choose Deny Claim. The Deny Claim section will appear below the header. Enter PX_R24040 in the reject code field. When the matching reject code appears in the dropdown list, select it and click Submit to apply the denial.
steps.checklistItem: Deny the claim using Reject code PX_R24040
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Deny Claim panel (which dispatches the deny_claim action).

steps.hint: Pick 'Deny' from the Decision dropdown in the claim header, then click Submit and confirm in the dialog.
steps.name: Submit Deny decision
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the Deny decision in the submit dialog.

description: Walk the Member Timely Filing SOP for a claim filed outside the 365-day TFL: confirm the benefit type (SPIDER), look up the member TFL on the Search → Benefits sub-tab, confirm the claim is Non-ITS Home, walk the corrected-claim (PX_PAJ + Frequency) and Sutter (PX_SUT) gates, verify provider participation, confirm all three claim lines fall outside the TFL, rule out a prior deleted claim within the TFL and Acceptable Proof, then deny with reject code PX_R24040.

stepSummaryForResults.name: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_MTF hard edit identified
Frequency not 7 — not a corrected claim
PX_SUT event absent — provider is not Sutter
All three claim lines outside the TFL
Deleted claim confirmed outside the TFL
No Acceptable Proof in PWK section
Deny Claim panel submitted with PX_R24040
